## Welcome

Call to order/Roll Call L. Marx calls to order the meeting at 12:04.

## Review and Adopt Agenda

- Committee reviewed the agenda; Chair Marx called for a motion to adopt the agenda.

## · Motion :

- o Jamie Alley motioned that the committee adopt the agenda.
- o Larry Marx seconded the motion.
- o 2 members present voted in favor; 0 abstained; motion carried.

## Review Role of Finance Committee

- -N. Kalfas went over bylaws and role of finance committee. Shared some charges of finance committee.
- -N. Kalfas explains some first items finance committees typically tackle. Fiscal year has been established. Budget is dependent on funding information. Bank account is dependent on secretariat. Secretariat RFP dependent on budget.
- -Fiscal policies are included in the packet to look at as examples.

Question J. Alley - Where do we start?

N. Kalfas - Recommends looking at sample budgets from other commissions, getting a secretariat and ED in place. Secretariat sometimes provides ED as their employee but the ED would still report to the commission.

## Discussion of Funding and Funding Processes

- -C. Sims is recognized as on the call to present. Committee reviews draft budgets from other commissions.
- o Typically it takes 3-7 months to get a budget going in other commissions. Others have delegated to the chair to draft a budget and then review it with the finance committee.
- o Future funding may include a fee component, other sources such as grants to balance out revenue sources. These are intermittent and not guaranteed.
- o Expenses include IT, staffing, ED, secretariat, legal services, insurance, data system
- o Finance Committee could put down some numbers and discuss items such as in-person vs virtual meetings, bank account (when secretariat is selected)
- -N. Kalfas points out line items in the ASLP budget
- o Administrative fee refers to bank account
- o Salaries and wages are for a part time ED
- o Travel budget is never realized, many do virtual or hybrid meetings

Question L. Marx - Asks about compact fees for participants

N. Kalfas - There are two fees, one to the commission most charge between $30 and $75, one the state chooses and charges. Most commissions suggest a fee to the states but the state does not have to take the suggestion.

C. Sims - The fee is typically equal to or less than what a singles state license would cost.

Question L. Marx - What is the cost for IT support?

C. Sims - $1.5 million for initial build. There are other options available for the PA Compact Commission to explore.

Question J. Alley - Are there renewal fees and does the commission set those? If the inital fee is set by state can the commission set the renewal fee?

N. Kalfas - There is leway to allow for renewal fees. The commission cannot set fees for states. The state sets their renewal fee but they typically look to other states.

Question J. Alley - Is the data system something we can look into now or wait?

- C. Sims - The other compacts get the secretariat and ED first but you can explore options now.
- J. Alley - It may be of interest to partner with one of the partners for secretariat and ED. Consider getting data system info along with secretariat and ED.
- N. Kalfas - There are many options for how to proceed with secretariat, ED and data system.
